explanation: Only temperature changes the value of the equilibrium constant K (adding catalyst, pressure, or reactants does not). Treat heat as a reagent: for an ENDOTHERMIC reaction heat is a reactant, so raising T shifts toward products and K increases; for an EXOTHERMIC reaction heat is a product, so raising T shifts toward reactants and K decreases. Quantitatively the van 't Hoff equation ln(K2/K1) = -(dH/R)(1/T2 - 1/T1) ties the direction of the shift to the sign of dH. On the AP exam, justify the direction with Le Chatelier and recognize that K is temperature-dependent. The animation recomputes K(T) and redraws the product/reactant split as you change T and toggle endo/exo.
bullets: Temperature is the ONLY factor that changes the numerical value of K.
Endothermic: heat is a reactant, so heating raises K (more products).
Exothermic: heat is a product, so heating lowers K (more reactants).
Bar split and molecule counts show the product fraction K/(1+K) shift.
